subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: Should OpenClaw's public web-tool egress boundary be a scoped `web_fetch` domain policy, a shared `web_fetch`/`web_search`/browser policy, or an operator-managed proxy contract?
rationale: This would add an operator-trusted security/config boundary, and the open related PRs encode different answers that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Define Shared Egress Contract
options.body: Set the cross-tool semantics first, including allow/deny precedence, redirects, caches, provider fallback, hosted search, browser navigation, proxy ownership, docs, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Land Scoped web_fetch First
options.body: Sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an interim contract while keeping deny domains, search, browser, and proxy coverage tracked separately.

options.title: Use Managed Proxy As Boundary
options.body: Make `proxy.enabled` plus external proxy policy the primary egress firewall and avoid adding local domain firewall semantics to web tools.

recommendation.title: Define Shared Egress Contract
recommendation.body: Set the cross-tool semantics first, including allow/deny precedence, redirects, caches, provider fallback, hosted search, browser navigation, proxy ownership, docs, and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest history across SSRF, guarded fetch, and web-tool security code paths implicated by this boundary choice.
